Controls for an MRQAP

Source: R/model_control.R, R/report_specify.R
control_mrqap.Rd

control_mrqap() sets the controls of estimate_mrqap(), checks each one, and returns them as an object of class mrqap_control. estimate_mrqap() passes its control argument through this function, so control = list(family = "poisson") and control = control_mrqap(family = "poisson") fit the same model. Calling control_mrqap() first shows the full set of controls, and finds a mistake before a long run starts. The tests, such as test_permutation(), read ncores, strategy, and seed from the same object, so one set of controls serves a model and a test alike.

A control that is not named keeps its default. A name that infernet used before is converted to its current name, with a warning. An option of another model that has no meaning in an MRQAP, such as goldfish's max_iterations, is dropped, with one warning that names each. The result of goldfish's set_algorithm_newton() or set_preprocessing() (or set_estimation_opt() before goldfish 2.0.0) can be given whole. Any other name aborts, and the nearest control is suggested.

Usage

control_mrqap(
  permute = c("predictor", "outcome"),
  family = c("auto", "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negbin", "zip"),
  directed = NULL,
  loops = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  ncores = NULL,
  strategy = NULL,
  use_robust_errors = FALSE,
  random_intercept_nets = FALSE,
  random_intercept_sender = FALSE,
  random_intercept_receiver = FALSE,
  random_intercept_reporter = FALSE,
  missing = "available",
  less_mem = FALSE,
  persist = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_control'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

permute

What the null distribution permutes. "predictor" (the default) residualises each main predictor against the others and permutes that residual, which is Dekker et al.'s (2007) double semi-partialling. "outcome" permutes the outcome and leaves the predictors alone. With one predictor there is nothing to residualise against, so "predictor" reduces to "outcome", and the model says so.

family

The family of the model. "auto" (the default) reads it from the outcome: "binomial" for a binary outcome, otherwise "gaussian", and says which. The others are "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negbin" (with {MASS}), and "zip", a zero-inflated Poisson (with {pscl}).

directed

Logical, whether a tie from i to j differs from one from j to i. NULL (the default) reads it from the network, and says so.

loops

Logical, whether loops, the ties from a node to itself, enter the model. NULL (the default) includes them only where the network has loops.

seed

A number to set the random seed with before the permutations, so that a fit can be reproduced. NULL (the default) leaves the seed as it is. The same seed gives the same result on any strategy.

groups

A vector with a group for each node, so that each node is permuted only among the nodes of its group. On a two-mode network, its length says which mode it groups. NULL (the default) permutes all nodes together.

ncores

A number of cores to run the permutations on. More than one runs them on that many "multisession" workers, and one runs them sequentially, whatever strategy says. NULL (the default) leaves the choice to strategy. A parallel run helps only where each permutation is costly: a family other than "gaussian", random intercepts, or a cognitive social structure, on a network of more than about 50 nodes, with 1,000 or more times. Elsewhere the start of the workers costs more than it saves: a gaussian model solves its design once, so each permutation is cheap. Give ncores rather than strategy = "multisession", which starts a worker on every core.

strategy

The {future} plan that the permutations run on where ncores is NULL: "sequential", "multisession", "multicore", or "cluster". The plan that was set before is restored after the fit. NULL (the default) uses the plan that was set with future::plan(), which is sequential unless it was changed. Set a plan once in a session, with future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2), and its workers start once, not once in each call.

use_robust_errors

Logical, whether to use HC3 robust standard errors for the observed model's t values. FALSE by default.

random_intercept_nets, random_intercept_sender, random_intercept_receiver, random_intercept_reporter

Logical, whether to fit an {lme4} random intercept for each network of a list, each sender, each receiver, or each reporter of a cognitive social structure. FALSE by default. In the formula, (1 | network), (1 | sender), (1 | receiver), and (1 | reporter) set the same controls.

missing

What to do with an unobserved dyad, that is, an NA in the outcome or in a predictor. "available" (the default) drops the dyad, and permutes nodes only among nodes with the same unobserved cells, so that every permutation is fitted on the same dyads as the observed model. "fail" stops instead, and names how many dyads are unobserved on each variable. See the section on missing data in estimate_mrqap().

less_mem

Logical, whether to leave the observed model object out of the result, to save memory on a large network. FALSE by default.

persist

Logical, whether the controls given in this call become the defaults of the session. See the section on persistent controls. FALSE by default, which changes nothing. Given as persist = FALSE, it clears the persistent controls.

...

Controls by another name: a name that infernet used before, or an option of another model. See the description.

x

An object of class mrqap_control.

Value

An object of class mrqap_control: a list with one element for each control. Its attribute source says whether each control was "given", comes from an "option", or keeps its "default". print() returns x, invisibly.

Persistent controls

control_mrqap(ncores = 2, missing = "fail", persist = TRUE) writes the controls that it is given to options(infernet.control), after it checks them. Each later call of estimate_mrqap(), test_random(), test_configuration(), test_permutation(), test_gof(), test_distributions(), test_parameter(), test_time(), and play_diffusions() then uses them as defaults, and says so with options(snet_verbosity = "verbose").

  • A control given in a call takes priority over a persistent one. Give strategy = NULL in a call to use the plan of future::plan() where a strategy or ncores persists.

  • A second call with persist = TRUE adds to the persistent controls, and replaces a control that it gives again. A control given as NULL, such as control_mrqap(ncores = NULL, persist = TRUE), is removed.

  • control_mrqap(persist = FALSE) clears all of them.

  • control_mrqap() shows the controls in force, and marks each one that comes from the persistent controls with (option).

  • control_mrqap() reads the persistent controls when it is called, so its result keeps the same controls if the options change later.

A seed can persist. Each call then sets the same seed, and so draws the same random numbers, which reproduces each result. The print of a result gives the seed that it used.

Every result records the controls that it used, as control (an attribute of a diffs_model). Give that record as control to fit the same model again without the options of the session.

References

Dekker, David, David Krackhardt, and Tom A.B. Snijders. 2007. "Sensitivity of MRQAP tests to collinearity and autocorrelation conditions." Psychometrika 72(4): 563-581. doi:10.1007/s11336-007-9016-1

See also

Other models: diagnose_confusion(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

control_mrqap(family = "poisson", seed = 1)
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 2 set, 13 at their defaults
#> 
#>   family  "poisson"
#>   seed    1
# A name that infernet used before is converted, with a warning
control_mrqap(nullhyp = "qapy")
#> Warning: `nullhyp = "qapy"` is now `permute = "outcome"`.
#> The control was renamed in infernet 0.2.0.
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 1 set, 14 at their defaults
#> 
#>   permute  "outcome"
# Controls that later calls use as defaults
control_mrqap(missing = "fail", seed = 1, persist = TRUE)
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 2 set, 13 at their defaults
#> 
#>   seed     1
#>   missing  "fail"
control_mrqap()
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 2 set, 13 at their defaults
#> 
#>   seed     1  (option)
#>   missing  "fail"  (option)
#> 
#> # (option) persists from control_mrqap(..., persist = TRUE);
#> #   control_mrqap(persist = FALSE) clears it.
control_mrqap(persist = FALSE)
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 0 set, 15 at their defaults
#>
